# Overview

The ClawInc OpenClaw stack runs on the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano — and in several respects it runs *better* than the DigitalOcean droplet used in the standard deployment. The Orin Nano has 8 GB of unified memory (versus 1 GB on the base droplet), an ARM64 CPU compatible with all required packages, and a built-in GPU available for future local-model extensions.

The only meaningful differences from the standard droplet install are:

1. **OS version.** JetPack 6.x ships Ubuntu 22.04, not 24.04. One PPA is needed for Python 3.12.
2. **Networking.** The Jetson is on your local network, not a public cloud IP. Telegram bots still work perfectly (long-polling is outbound). The Shiny dashboard is LAN-accessible by default; Tailscale makes it reachable from anywhere.
3. **Swap.** Not needed on the 8 GB model. Keep it on the 4 GB model.

---

# Compatibility Matrix

| Component | DO Droplet | Jetson Orin Nano | Compatible |
|-----------|-----------|-------------------|:----------:|
| Node.js 24 | x86\_64 | aarch64 | Yes |
| OpenClaw (npm) | x86\_64 | aarch64 | Yes — pure JavaScript |
| Shiny for Python | x86\_64 | aarch64 | Yes — ARM64 pip wheels |
| psutil | x86\_64 | aarch64 | Yes |
| systemd | Ubuntu 24.04 | Ubuntu 22.04 (JetPack 6) | Yes |
| Telegram long-polling | public IP | local network | Yes — outbound HTTPS only |
| Shiny dashboard (public) | port 8050 open | LAN only by default | Partial — see Section 6 |

---

# Before You Begin

## Check Your JetPack Version

```bash
cat /etc/nv_tegra_release
# or
dpkg -l | grep jetpack
```

- **JetPack 6.x** = Ubuntu 22.04 (recommended — these instructions target this version)
- **JetPack 5.x** = Ubuntu 20.04 (also works; same steps apply)

## 4 GB vs 8 GB Model

| | 4 GB model | 8 GB model |
|--|-----------|-----------|
| Keep 2 GB swap step | Yes | Optional |
| All 5 agents comfortable | Tight | Yes |
| `MemoryMax` in systemd service | Keep at 512 M | Can raise to 1 G |

The Orin Nano uses **unified memory** — the CPU and GPU share the same pool — so 8 GB goes a long way even with Node.js running five concurrent LLM sessions.

---

# Step 1 — Clone the Repository

Install Git if not already present, then clone the ClawInc repo directly onto the Jetson.

```bash
sudo apt-get install -y git
git clone https://github.com/westland/ClawInc.git
cd ClawInc
```

All subsequent steps assume your working directory is `~/ClawInc`.

---

# Step 2 — Fill In Your Credentials

Open the deploy script and edit the **CONFIGURATION** block at the top (lines 5–15). Replace every `YOUR_*` placeholder with your real keys.

```bash
nano deploy/deploy-openclaw.sh
```

You will need:

- **Anthropic API key** — from [console.anthropic.com](https://console.anthropic.com)
- **Four Telegram bot tokens** — one each for Henry, Coder, Scout, and Writer (create via [@BotFather](https://t.me/BotFather))

```bash
# CONFIGURATION — fill these in before running
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="sk-ant-..."

TELEGRAM_TOKEN_HENRY="123456:ABC..."
TELEGRAM_TOKEN_CODER="123456:ABC..."
TELEGRAM_TOKEN_SCOUT="123456:ABC..."
TELEGRAM_TOKEN_WRITER="123456:ABC..."
TELEGRAM_TOKEN_WATCHER="123456:ABC..."   # Watcher has no Telegram bot; token optional
```

Save and exit (`Ctrl+O`, `Ctrl+X`).

---

# Step 3 — Run the Deploy Script

The script was written for Ubuntu 24.04 but is fully compatible with 22.04. Run it as root.

```bash
sudo bash deploy/deploy-openclaw.sh
```

The script will:

- Create 2 GB swap (skip on 8 GB model if preferred — see note at start of script)
- Install Node.js 24 via NodeSource (ARM64 build)
- Install OpenClaw globally via npm
- Create the `clawuser` service account
- Copy all five agent workspaces to `/home/clawuser/.openclaw/`
- Substitute your API keys into the config
- Install and start the `openclaw.service` systemd unit
- Add six cron jobs (morning research, daily memo, overnight dev, health checks, R&D, cleanup)

**Expected runtime:** 8–12 minutes (dominated by `apt-get update` and `npm install -g openclaw`).

> **Note:** If the script errors on a step involving `python3.12`, that is expected on Ubuntu 22.04.
> Continue to Step 4 — the OpenClaw gateway itself does not require Python.

---

# Step 4 — Install Python 3.12 for the Shiny Dashboard

Ubuntu 22.04 ships Python 3.10 by default. Python 3.12 is available via the **deadsnakes PPA**.

```bash
sudo add-apt-repository ppa:deadsnakes/ppa -y
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y python3.12 python3.12-venv python3.12-distutils
```

Now create the dashboard virtual environment and install dependencies:

```bash
sudo mkdir -p /opt/clawinc-dashboard
sudo python3.12 -m venv /opt/clawinc-dashboard/venv
sudo /opt/clawinc-dashboard/venv/bin/pip install shiny psutil
```

Copy the dashboard app from the cloned repo:

```bash
sudo cp ~/ClawInc/dashboard/app.py /opt/clawinc-dashboard/
```

Install and start the systemd service:

```bash
sudo cp ~/ClawInc/deploy/clawinc-dashboard.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable clawinc-dashboard
sudo systemctl start clawinc-dashboard
```

---

# Step 5 — Configure the Firewall

```bash
sudo ufw allow ssh
sudo ufw allow 8050/tcp    # Shiny dashboard
sudo ufw --force enable
sudo ufw status
```

Expected output:

```
Status: active

To                    Action      From
--                    ------      ----
22/tcp                ALLOW       Anywhere
8050/tcp              ALLOW       Anywhere
```

> The OpenClaw gateway (port 18789) is **not** opened in UFW — it binds to
> `127.0.0.1` only and is accessed via SSH tunnel. This matches the security
> model of the cloud deployment.

---

# Step 6 — Verify Everything Is Running

```bash
systemctl is-active openclaw            # should print: active
systemctl is-active clawinc-dashboard   # should print: active

sudo -u clawuser openclaw status
sudo -u clawuser openclaw cron list
```

The `openclaw cron list` command should display all six scheduled jobs with their next run times.

Check memory and swap:

```bash
free -h
# 8 GB model — no swap needed
# 4 GB model — should show 2 GB swap from deploy script
```

---

# Step 7 — Access Your Dashboards

## Find the Jetson's Local IP

```bash
ip addr show | grep "inet " | grep -v 127.0.0.1
# Example output: inet 192.168.1.42/24 brd 192.168.1.255 scope global eth0
```

## Shiny Monitoring Dashboard

Open directly in any browser on the same network — no SSH, no token required:

```
http://JETSON_LAN_IP:8050
```

For example: `http://192.168.1.42:8050`

The dashboard shows all five agent cards, CPU/RAM/disk gauges, Telegram bot bindings, cron schedule, and a live activity log. It auto-refreshes every 30 seconds.

## OpenClaw Control UI (Admin)

The Control UI requires an SSH tunnel because the gateway is bound to localhost.

**Step 1** — Open the tunnel from your laptop (leave this terminal open):

```bash
ssh -N -L 18789:127.0.0.1:18789 YOUR_USERNAME@JETSON_LAN_IP
```

**Step 2** — Get the tokenized URL from the Jetson:

```bash
sudo -u clawuser openclaw dashboard
# Outputs: http://localhost:18789/#token=<your-token>
```

**Step 3** — Open that URL in your browser. The token is embedded — no manual paste needed.

---

# Step 8 — Remote Access Outside Your LAN (Optional)

By default the Jetson is only accessible on your local network. For classroom use where students need to reach their bots from anywhere, **Tailscale** is the simplest solution.

## Install Tailscale

```bash
curl -fsSL https://tailscale.com/install.sh | sh
sudo tailscale up
tailscale ip -4    # prints something like 100.x.x.x
```

Sign in with a free Tailscale account. Once connected, every device on your Tailscale network can reach the Jetson at its stable Tailscale IP — no router port-forwarding required.

## Access With Tailscale

| Resource | URL |
|----------|-----|
| Shiny dashboard | `http://100.x.x.x:8050` |
| OpenClaw Control UI | SSH tunnel via Tailscale IP, then `localhost:18789` |
| SSH | `ssh username@100.x.x.x` |

> **Telegram bots are unaffected by any of this.** Long-polling is outbound HTTPS
> from the Jetson to Telegram's servers. The bots respond to messages regardless
> of whether Tailscale is installed.

# Useful Commands

## Service Management

```bash
# OpenClaw gateway
systemctl status openclaw
systemctl restart openclaw
journalctl -u openclaw -f          # tail logs in real time

# Shiny dashboard
systemctl status clawinc-dashboard
systemctl restart clawinc-dashboard
journalctl -u clawinc-dashboard -f
```

## Agent Management

```bash
sudo -u clawuser openclaw status
sudo -u clawuser openclaw cron list
sudo -u clawuser openclaw doctor

# Get dashboard tokenized URL
sudo -u clawuser openclaw dashboard

# Search an agent's memory
sudo -u clawuser openclaw memory search "marketing strategy" --agent henry

# Manually trigger an agent
sudo -u clawuser openclaw chat henry "run the daily standup"
```

## Updating from GitHub

To pull the latest version of the repo and restart services:

```bash
cd ~/ClawInc
git pull origin main

# If dashboard/app.py changed:
sudo cp dashboard/app.py /opt/clawinc-dashboard/
sudo systemctl restart clawinc-dashboard

# If deploy/clawinc-dashboard.service changed:
sudo cp deploy/clawinc-dashboard.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl restart clawinc-dashboard
```

---

# Differences Summary: Jetson vs DigitalOcean

| | DigitalOcean Droplet | Jetson Orin Nano |
|--|---------------------|-----------------|
| **Architecture** | x86\_64 | aarch64 |
| **OS** | Ubuntu 24.04 | Ubuntu 22.04 (JetPack 6) |
| **RAM** | 1 GB + 2 GB swap | 4 or 8 GB unified |
| **Python 3.12** | Available natively | Requires deadsnakes PPA |
| **Public IP** | Yes | No (LAN only by default) |
| **Telegram bots** | Work immediately | Work immediately (outbound HTTPS) |
| **Shiny dashboard** | Public on port 8050 | LAN on port 8050; Tailscale for remote |
| **Monthly cost** | \$6 | \$0 (hardware already owned) |
| **GPU** | None | 1024 CUDA cores (future use) |

---

# Troubleshooting

## OpenClaw service fails to start

```bash
journalctl -u openclaw -n 50 --no-pager
```

The most common cause is a config validation error. Check with:

```bash
sudo -u clawuser openclaw config validate
```

## `openclaw cron list` returns "gateway token missing"

The gateway token needs to be set in both `auth.token` and `remote.token` in `openclaw.json`. Run:

```bash
TOKEN=$(python3 -c "
import json
with open('/home/clawuser/.openclaw/openclaw.json') as f:
    d = json.load(f)
print(d['gateway']['auth']['token'])
")
echo "Token is: $TOKEN"
```

Then edit `/home/clawuser/.openclaw/openclaw.json` and ensure `gateway.remote.token` matches `gateway.auth.token`.

## Shiny dashboard not reachable

```bash
systemctl is-active clawinc-dashboard
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://localhost:8050/
ufw status | grep 8050
```

All three should show: `active`, `200`, and a ALLOW rule for port 8050.

## Node.js install fails on ARM64

Verify the architecture before installing:

```bash
uname -m    # should print: aarch64
```

NodeSource explicitly supports aarch64 for Node.js 24. If the install script fails, try the manual method:

```bash
NODE_VERSION=24
ARCH=arm64
curl -fsSL https://nodejs.org/dist/latest-v${NODE_VERSION}.x/node-v${NODE_VERSION}.*-linux-${ARCH}.tar.xz \
  -o /tmp/node.tar.xz
tar -xJf /tmp/node.tar.xz -C /usr/local --strip-components=1
```
